Looking at my land and what I know from farming here in Quzhou my whole life, I'll do what my father did and what everyone around me does: winter wheat, then summer maize on the same ground. I have about 10 mu. I don't know much else that sells reliably at the market, and the grain station buys it every season.

For wheat, I'll plough the ground deep before planting in October like always. I'll buy the improved seed from the township supply station — not the old seeds, those yield less. I'll put down plenty of fertilizer at planting and again at jointing stage. Irrigation I'll do about four times: before winter sets in, at jointing, at heading, and at grain filling. If I water less the yield drops and I can't afford that. I'll spray herbicide early and maybe a fungicide if I see rust like last year.

After wheat harvest in June, I'll plant hybrid maize right away with rotary tillage. I won't waste time. Maize is easier — it rains more in summer so I only need to irrigate once or twice if there's drought. I'll apply fertilizer in two goes. One or two pesticide sprays for fall armyworm and corn borer.

I won't experiment. My margins are thin and I have a family. I do what works.
